args.title: checkout-api: unhealthy deploy v2.3.1 rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in production following the latest deploy. At detection, all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running v2.3.1 with healthy=false and an error rate of ~18% (0.18).

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy status in production (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy). The first rollback attempt failed partway — the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the service mixed (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry of the rollback to v2.3.0 completed successfully across all regions.

Current state: All production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate ~0.2% (0.002).

Impact: Elevated error rate (~18%) in checkout-api across all regions during the v2.3.1 deployment window.

Follow-up: Root cause of the v2.3.1 health-check failures is not yet identified; v2.3.1 should not be re-deployed without investigation and change-manager approval. Verify the rollback stability and confirm no lasting data/transaction impact from the elevated error period.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did go through despite the timeout (INC-0001, open) — no retry needed, and the idempotency key would have prevented a duplicate.

## Summary

**Rollback complete.** checkout-api is healthy in all production regions again.

**What I found:**
- All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were on **v2.3.1**, unhealthy, with an **18% error rate**.
- Release history: v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy). There was also a `v2.3.1-rc` in **staging** that was unhealthy — correctly excluded, since it was never a production release. The most recent production-healthy version was **v2.3.0**.

**What I did:**
1. Rolled back to **v2.3.0** — this is a previously-healthy production version, so no change-manager approval was required.
2. First attempt **failed partially**: the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the fleet split (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1). I checked status to confirm the real state rather than assuming the rollback had failed outright, then retried.
3. Retry succeeded: all three regions now on **v2.3.0**, `healthy: true`, error rate **0.2%** (down from 18%).
4. Opened **SEV2 incident INC-0001** documenting the deploy failure, the partial-failure and retry, current state, impact, and follow-up. The create call timed out at 30s but had in fact succeeded — I verified via `list_incidents` instead of blindly retrying.

**Two things worth flagging:**
- The root cause of the v2.3.1 health-check failures is **not yet identified**. v2.3.1 should not be re-deployed without investigation and change-manager approval.
- The ~18% error window means some checkout transactions likely failed. Someone should confirm whether there was customer-facing or data impact during that period — I noted this in the incident as a follow-up rather than guessing at it.
